title: Around town: autos, cabs & the metro
goal: Agree a fare with an auto driver, tell a driver where to turn and where to stop, ask how long a trip takes, book a cab and find your way on the metro or bus.
intro:
Getting around a Punjabi city means autos, e-rickshaws, cabs booked on an app and, on trips to Delhi, the metro. This unit gives you everything you'll say from the back seat: the fare (**ਕਿੰਨਾ ਲਓਗੇ?**), the route (**ਲਾਈਟਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਸੱਜੇ ਮੋੜ ਲਓ**), and where to get out (**ਬੱਸ, ਇੱਥੇ ਹੀ ਰੋਕ ਦਿਓ**).

The grammar is what makes those requests sound natural: **compound verbs** like ਰੋਕ **ਦਿਓ**, ਮੋੜ **ਲਓ**, ਬੈਠ **ਜਾਓ** — a second verb that tells you who the action is for and whether it's finished — and **ਲੱਗਣਾ** for 'it takes (time)'.

grammar.title: Compound verbs: ਰੋਕ ਦਿਓ, ਮੋੜ ਲਓ, ਬੈਠ ਜਾਓ
grammar.body:
Punjabi often adds a second verb — **ਦੇਣਾ, ਲੈਣਾ** or **ਜਾਣਾ** — to the bare stem of the main verb. The main verb carries the meaning; the second one (which takes all the endings) adds direction and a sense of 'done'. You've already met some: ਹੋ ਗਿਆ, ਖਾ ਲਿਆ, ਬੰਦ ਕਰ ਦਿਓ.

**stem + ਦੇਣਾ** — the action goes out from you, often for someone else: **ਰੋਕ ਦਿਓ** 'stop (for me)', **ਛੱਡ ਦਿਓ** 'drop me (off)', **ਉਤਾਰ ਦਿਓ** 'let me out', **ਪਹੁੰਚਾ ਦਿਓ** 'get me there', **ਦੱਸ ਦਿਓ** 'let me know'.
**stem + ਲੈਣਾ** — the action is for yourself or comes back to you: **ਮੋੜ ਲਓ** 'turn (your car)', **ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ ਲੈ** 'book (it for us)', **ਲੈ ਲਓ** 'take it'.
**stem + ਜਾਣਾ** — a change of place or state, with intransitive verbs: **ਬੈਠ ਜਾਓ** 'get in, sit down', **ਉਤਰ ਜਾਓ** 'get out', **ਰੁਕ ਜਾਓ** 'stop!', **ਪਹੁੰਚ ਜਾਵਾਂਗੇ** 'we'll get there'.

**Why bother?** The plain imperative (ਰੋਕੋ, ਉਤਾਰੋ) sounds abrupt, like an order shouted in an emergency. The compound is the normal, polite way to ask a driver: ਭਾਜੀ, ਇੱਥੇ ਰੋਕ ਦਿਓ.

The trap: compounds are for things that **happen**. In negatives use the simple verb: ਇੱਥੇ **ਨਾ ਰੋਕੋ** 'don't stop here' — not ਨਾ ਰੋਕ ਦਿਓ.

grammar.title: It takes (time): ਲੱਗਣਾ
grammar.body:
To say how long something takes, Punjabi makes **the time the subject of ਲੱਗਣਾ** ('to be applied, to be spent'), so the verb agrees with the amount of time:

ਇੱਕ ਘੰਟਾ **ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ** 'it takes an hour' (ਘੰਟਾ m sg)
ਵੀਹ ਮਿੰਟ **ਲੱਗਦੇ ਹਨ** 'it takes twenty minutes' (m pl)
ਬਹੁਤ ਦੇਰ **ਲੱਗੇਗੀ** 'it'll take ages' (ਦੇਰ f)
**ਕਿੰਨਾ ਟਾਈਮ ਲੱਗੇਗਾ?** 'how long will it take?'

The person it takes goes in **ਨੂੰ**: **ਮੈਨੂੰ** ਦੋ ਘੰਟੇ **ਲੱਗੇ** 'it took me two hours'. For a general fact add ਜਾਂਦਾ: ਇੱਕ ਘੰਟਾ ਲੱਗ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ 'it ends up taking an hour'.

**Money works the same way**: ਕਿੰਨੇ ਪੈਸੇ **ਲੱਗਣਗੇ**? 'how much will it cost?', ਸੌ ਰੁਪਏ ਲੱਗੇ 'it cost a hundred'.

**Distance** is simpler: ਕਿੰਨੀ ਦੂਰ ਹੈ? — ਪੰਜ ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ (ਹੈ). From … to …: ਇੱਥੋਂ ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ ਤੱਕ.

In everyday Punjabi you'll also hear the short future in **-ੂ**: ਦਸ ਮਿੰਟ **ਲੱਗੂ** 'it'll take ten minutes', ਉਹ ਆਊ 'he'll come' — very common in speech, but write ਲੱਗੇਗਾ.

The trap: don't make 'it' or the traveller the subject. Not ~~ਮੈਂ ਦੋ ਘੰਟੇ ਲੱਗਿਆ~~ — it's ਮੈਨੂੰ ਦੋ ਘੰਟੇ ਲੱਗੇ.

culture: In Punjabi cities the **auto** and the **ਈ-ਰਿਕਸ਼ਾ** are everywhere, and unless there's a working meter (rare outside big cities) you agree the fare **before** you get in. Haggling is expected and good-humoured: name your price, mention what you usually pay, and meet in the middle. Drivers are addressed as **ਭਾਜੀ**, **ਵੀਰ ਜੀ** or **ਭਾਈ ਸਾਹਬ**, an older one as **ਸਰਦਾਰ ਜੀ** or **ਅੰਕਲ ਜੀ**; they'll call a young woman **ਭੈਣ ਜੀ** and an older one **ਬੀਬੀ ਜੀ** or **ਆਂਟੀ ਜੀ**. Shared autos pick up extra **ਸਵਾਰੀਆਂ** along a fixed route for a few rupees each. App cabs work in Chandigarh, Mohali, Ludhiana and Amritsar; you'll still often get a call from the driver asking **ਕਿੱਥੇ ਆਵਾਂ?** 'where shall I come?'. Directions are given by landmarks, not street names — **ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ, ਪੈਟਰੋਲ ਪੰਪ ਦੇ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ**, **ਲਾਈਟਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਖੱਬੇ** — and Chandigarh people navigate by sector number (*ਸੈਕਟਰ ਸਤਾਰਾਂ*). Amritsar has its BRTS 'metro bus'; the nearest real metro is in Delhi, where Punjabi is heard on every line.

lessons.title: Agreeing the fare

tip.title: Asking the price and haggling
tip.body:
- Ask with the future: X ਦਾ **ਕਿੰਨਾ ਲਓਗੇ?** 'how much will you take for X?', or X **ਚੱਲੋਗੇ?** 'will you go to X?'
- Counter with **ਲੈ ਲਓ**: ਸੌ ਰੁਪਏ ਲੈ ਲਓ 'take a hundred'.
- Address the driver as **ਭਾਜੀ** or **ਵੀਰ ਜੀ**, and use ਤੁਸੀਂ forms.

tip.title: Stop, drop me, get out: compound verbs
tip.body:
- **ਦੇਣਾ** when you do it for someone: ਰੋਕ **ਦਿਓ** 'stop (for me)', ਉਤਾਰ **ਦਿਓ** 'drop me'.
- **ਲੈਣਾ** when it's for yourself: ਮੋੜ **ਲਓ**, ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ **ਲੈ**.
- **ਜਾਣਾ** for getting in, out, there: ਬੈਠ **ਜਾਓ**, ਉਤਰ **ਜਾਓ**.
- In 'don't', use the simple verb: ਇੱਥੇ ਨਾ **ਰੋਕੋ**.

tip.title: Turning: ਮੋੜ ਲਓ vs ਮੁੜ ਜਾਓ
tip.body:
- **ਮੋੜਨਾ** = turn something (the car): ਗੱਡੀ ਸੱਜੇ **ਮੋੜ ਲਓ**.
- **ਮੁੜਨਾ** = turn yourself: ਸੱਜੇ **ਮੁੜ ਜਾਓ** (on foot).
- Where to turn takes **ਤੋਂ**: ਲਾਈਟਾਂ **ਤੋਂ** ਖੱਬੇ 'left at the lights'.
- ਲਾਈਟਾਂ is feminine plural: **ਅਗਲੀਆਂ** ਲਾਈਟਾਂ.
tip.pattern: place + ਤੋਂ + ਸੱਜੇ / ਖੱਬੇ + ਮੋੜ ਲਓ

tip.title: It takes…: ਲੱਗਣਾ
tip.body:
- The time is the subject of **ਲੱਗਣਾ**, and the verb agrees with it: ਇੱਕ ਘੰਟਾ **ਲੱਗਦਾ** ਹੈ, ਵੀਹ ਮਿੰਟ **ਲੱਗਦੇ** ਹਨ, ਦੇਰ (f) **ਲੱਗੇਗੀ**.
- The person it takes gets **ਨੂੰ**: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਦੋ ਘੰਟੇ **ਲੱਗੇ** 'it took me two hours'.
- Cost works the same way: ਕਿੰਨੇ ਪੈਸੇ **ਲੱਗਣਗੇ**?
tip.pattern: (X ਨੂੰ) + time + ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ / ਲੱਗਦੇ ਹਨ

lessons.title: Booking a cab

tip.title: English verbs: ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ ਲੈ, ਕੈਂਸਲ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ
tip.body:
- App words take **ਕਰਨਾ** + a compound: ਕੈਬ ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ **ਲੈ** (for us), ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ **ਦਿੱਤੀ** (done!).
- With ਨੇ the verb agrees with the thing: ਕੈਬ (f) ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ **ਦਿੱਤੀ**, ਆਟੋ (m) ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ **ਦਿੱਤਾ**.
- 'It gets booked' = **ਬੁੱਕ ਹੋ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ**.
tip.pattern: ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ ਲੈ · ਬੁੱਕ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ · ਬੁੱਕ ਹੋ ਗਈ

new: ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ ਤੇਜ਼ ਚਲਾਓ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਦੇਰ ਹੋ ਰਹੀ ਹੈ।

tip.title: Which one? ਕਿਹੜਾ agrees
tip.body:
- **ਕਿਹੜਾ** 'which' agrees like an adjective: ਕਿਹੜਾ ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ, **ਕਿਹੜੀ** ਮੈਟਰੋ, and before a postposition **ਕਿਹੜੇ**: ਕਿਹੜੇ ਪਲੇਟਫ਼ਾਰਮ ਤੋਂ?
- 'Have to change' = **ਬਦਲਣੀ ਪਵੇਗੀ** — the infinitive agrees with what you change (ਮੈਟਰੋ f).
- **ਉਤਰਨਾ ਹੈ** 'I need to get off'.
